sections.heading: C — Driving basics and sharing the road
sections.markdown:
## C — Driving basics and sharing the road

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A16
Start per the owner manual with the parking brake set, a stick shift out of gear with clutch down as needed, and an automatic selector in park. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]
FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A16
Feed speed in gently since hard launches spin wheels and slide cars, and rehearse clutch and throttle so shifts neither race nor stall. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]
FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A16
Grip the wheel at eight to ten left and two to four right, hand over hand through sharp bends while straightening manually, or push pull with outward knuckles and uncrossed hands. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]
FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A16
Scan ahead, aside and astern always, holding eyes twelve seconds out, about a city block downtown or four blocks on highways, timed by counting thousands to a fixed object. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]
FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A16
Favor side glances at crossings and lane moves and rear checks in dense traffic, lane shifts, slowdowns, reversing and long descents. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]
FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A17
Enter crossings only after left right scans, cede left turns to all oncoming traffic including bikes while rechecking twice, and turn right solely past clear lefts, clear paths, patient bikes and legal reds. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A17
Trust no signal blindly, scan even fresh greens, halt for dead lights as for stop signs, creep out past blind corners, and never strand the car blocking the box. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A17
Slow and sweep both rail directions at every crossing with far side room assured, and past multi track trains linger until the first clears sight of a second. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A17
Work zones speak through orange and black roadside boards on the right, or both sides when divided, and post lower limits that rule unless absent. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A17
Zone speeding, disobedience, lane abuse or worker endangerment can cost a thousand dollars plus points and retraining, with handheld phone fines doubled inside. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A17
Through zones slow down, heed boards and flaggers, respect shifting lanes, and drive nights with extreme care whether crews show or not. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A18
Also watch brake lights ahead, merge early, slide from workers, shun tailgates, honor mobile crews to the End Road Work board, drop distractions, detour when able, and bank extra time calmly. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A18
Careless harm to walkers, riders, wheelchair users, animal traffic, road crews, garbage, tank, mail and express haulers draws stiffer penalties, and every pass must leave three feet. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A18
Sirens and red or blue flashers command a right edge stop held until passage unless officers wave on, while any roadside stop demands slowing below the limit plus one lane over when safe. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A18
Walkers own every crosswalk, painted or sidewalk implied, once a raised hand or any body part or aid enters its mouth, and doors must never strike people, bikes or traffic. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A18
Guard hardest for children near schools, stops, parks and ice cream trucks plus every driveway reversal, obey posted school limits, and halt for crossing pupils and guard signals. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A18
White canes and guide dogs always win the right of way with full stops held until the road clears, greens notwithstanding at regulated corners. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A19
Bikes count as vehicles owning lanes outright when narrow, while unskilled wobblers ignoring signs and night lights deserve widened caution. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]
FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A19
Riders keep right as safe, may hold a right turn lane left edge going straight, obey signs with hand signals, yield to walkers, helmet under sixteen, and dress bright with lights and tuned machines. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]
FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A19
Drivers yield to bikes at crossings, paths and pre turn cuts under doubled failure fines, pass slow with three feet minding width and loads, then avoid quick slows, stops and right hooks plus needless horn blasts. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]
FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A19
Turning drivers hunt for bikes and sidewalk children, never slice or shoulder riders off, expect wrong way wheels and sloppy wet handling, may pass safely inside no passing zones, and keep bike lanes, doors and reverse paths bike checked. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]
FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A20
Motorcyclists have the right to a full lane and two motorcycles may share one lane; check mirrors and blind spots by turning your head, and look carefully before turning left because about half of motorcycle crashes involve another motor vehicle and nearly forty percent are caused by that vehicle turning left in front of the motorcyclist [A20].
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]
FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A20
Distrust lingering bike blinkers, telegraph every move, gift room for pothole dodges, trail three to four seconds or longer when wet, dip beams, and hold course while being passed. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]
FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A20
Expect sluggish trucks and tractors on grades, yield to signaling buses, grant orange triangle rigs under twenty five miles per hour room, and pass slow traffic lawfully even over double yellow with clear sight. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]
FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A20
Never outdrive vision: pick a far fixed mark and if it arrives before four counted thousands, shed speed at once. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]
FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A20
Lit ice cream trucks with arms out force a ten foot stop fore or aft, then five mile per hour creeping yielded to crossing children, except across islands or barriers. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]
FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A20
Horses travel single file rightward, and drivers must slow or halt with gentle space and silence, never horns or startling din. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]
FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A21
Big rig side blind zones swallow cars unseen in driver mirrors, and tailgating their rears blinds both parties to forward trouble, so hold real following gaps. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]
FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A21
Sixty five foot rigs stopping on doubled room punish cut ins, so reenter only past full fronts in mirrors without slowing, and never wedge beside wide swinging turns blind twenty feet fore and two hundred aft. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]
FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A20
Trucks crawl uphill, swing wide, brake long and tip tall, so human error by car drivers can still wreck the evading trucker: shun every No-Zone [A20] [A21].
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]
FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A21
Pass trucks solely with room sans speeding, checked mirrors, legal ground, brisk cab clearance, mirror confirmed reentry right, and sustained pace after. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]
